result.instructions: Tools for Billetweb, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "How many tickets are left for my next event?"; "Who has not checked in yet for Saturday's session?"; "How much did I sell last month and when is my next payout?". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Billetweb data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run billetweb_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run billetweb_request_feature to record the request. Paid plans: Pro (10,000 tool calls a month, $9/month or $90/year, for normal use) and Pro+ (100,000 tool calls a month, $39/month or $390/year, for automations and heavy use). A plan can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run billetweb_upgrade without a plan: it returns both plans, each with a payment link for the user to open. billetweb_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: billetweb_list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: List the organiser's events with id, name, start/end, place, shop URL, online state, tax rate, tags and contact. Past events are left out unless include_past is set. GET /events.

include_past.description: Also return past events (default: only current and upcoming).

limit.description: Billetweb does not page its lists; at most this many rows are returned (default 100, max 500); the reply says when it was cut.

tools.name: billetweb_get_availability
tools.title: Get availability
tools.description: Remaining places of an event: per session, per category and per ticket type, with avail (-1 = unlimited), quota and sales. Use it to answer 'how many seats are left'. GET /event/{id}/avail.

session.description: A session id or start time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM). Without it, all sessions of a multi-session event.

include_carts.description: Count carts in progress as taken (temp=1).

tools.name: billetweb_list_tickets
tools.title: List ticket types
tools.description: The ticket types (tarifs) of an event in display order: id, name, price, category, quota, visibility (0 visible, 1 web, 2 box office, 3 secret link, 4 hidden), sales window, tax and commission. GET /event/{id}/tickets.

limit.description: Billetweb does not page its lists; at most this many rows are returned (default 200, max 1000); the reply says when it was cut.

tools.name: billetweb_list_sessions
tools.title: List sessions
tools.description: The sessions (séances, dates) of a multi-session event: id, start/end, name, place, quota, total_sales, state (0 open, 1 hidden, 2 box office only, 3 web only, 4 link only, 5 cancelled) and the ticket ids sold in it. GET /event/{id}/dates.

state.description: Only sessions in this state (0 open, 1 hidden, 2 box office, 3 web, 4 link, 5 cancelled).

ended_within_days.description: Sessions that ended in the last N days.

start_from.description: Only sessions starting at or after this moment (yyyy-mm-dd or ISO 8601 date-time with timezone).

start_to.description: Only sessions starting at or before this moment.

limit.description: Billetweb does not page its lists; at most this many rows are returned (default 200, max 1000); the reply says when it was cut.

tools.name: billetweb_list_attendees
tools.title: List attendees of an event
tools.description: The attendees (one row per ticket) of one event: name, email, ticket type, price, check-in state (used), session, order id and payment, custom form answers. Filter by session, ticket, buyer, check-in state or when the order changed; use updated_since to fetch only what is new. Billetweb allows 10 attendees calls per minute (shared with billetweb_list_all_attendees), so prefer one filtered call. GET /event/{id}/attendees.

only_future_sessions.description: Only sessions that have not passed.

barcode.description: Only the ticket with this barcode.

updated_since.description: Only orders created or modified after this moment (yyyy-mm-dd or ISO 8601 date-time with timezone).

updated_within_minutes.description: Only orders created or modified in the last N minutes.

updated_before.description: Only orders created or modified before this moment.

created_from.description: Only orders created on or after this date (yyyy-mm-dd).

created_to.description: Only orders created on or before this date, whole day included (yyyy-mm-dd).

used.description: Ticket state: 0 not checked in, 1 checked in, 2 checked out, 3 expired.

ticket_id.description: Only this ticket type (tarif) id, from billetweb_list_tickets.

include_refunded.description: Also return refunded or cancelled tickets.

only_refunded.description: Return only refunded or cancelled tickets.

include_links.description: Keep the per-ticket download / manage-order links (default: dropped, they open the buyer's ticket).

limit.description: Billetweb does not page its lists; at most this many rows are returned (default 50, max 500); the reply says when it was cut.

tools.name: billetweb_list_all_attendees
tools.title: List attendees across all events
tools.description: The attendees of ALL events, newest changes included, with the same fields as billetweb_list_attendees. Filter by event tag, only unfinished events, buyer, ticket, check-in state or order change time. Billetweb allows 10 attendees calls per minute; use updated_since for incremental reads. GET /attendees.

only_unfinished_events.description: Only events that are not over.

updated_within_minutes.description: Only orders created or modified in the last N minutes.

created_from.description: Only orders created on or after this date (yyyy-mm-dd).

ticket_id.description: Only this ticket type (tarif) id, from billetweb_list_tickets.

include_refunded.description: Also return refunded or cancelled tickets.

include_links.description: Keep the per-ticket download / manage-order links (default: dropped, they open the buyer's ticket).

tools.name: billetweb_list_waiting_list
tools.title: List waiting list
tools.description: People on the waiting list of an event: name, email, phone, ticket/session wanted, places asked for and whether they were notified. GET /event/{id}/waiting.

limit.description: Billetweb does not page its lists; at most this many rows are returned (default 100, max 1000); the reply says when it was cut.

tools.name: billetweb_list_accounting
tools.title: List sales and refunds (accounting)
tools.description: The accounting history: one row per ticket and per money movement, type product_pay (sale) or product_refund (negative price), with price incl. tax, Billetweb fees, tax, payment type, transaction id and payout id (0 = not paid out yet). Period at most 1 year, starting at most 1 year ago. GET /accounting.

start.description: Start of the period (yyyy-mm-dd or ISO 8601 date-time with timezone).

channel.description: Only online (web) sales, or only the other channels (box office, offline orders).

limit.description: Billetweb does not page its lists; at most this many rows are returned (default 200, max 2000); the reply says when it was cut.

tools.name: billetweb_list_payouts
tools.title: List payouts
tools.description: The bank transfers Billetweb made to the organiser (type out) or took back (type in, negative amount): id, date, net amount, account holder. The IBAN is masked to its last 4 characters. GET /payouts.

date.description: Only the payouts of this day (yyyy-mm-dd).

limit.description: Billetweb does not page its lists; at most this many rows are returned (default 100, max 1000); the reply says when it was cut.

tools.name: billetweb_get_payout
tools.title: Get payout detail
tools.description: The line-by-line detail of one payout: each sale, refund or transfer with ticket reference, order, event, price, fees and tax. Net transferred = sum of price minus sum of fees. Pass a payout id, or a date (yyyy-mm-dd) for all payouts of that day. GET /payout/{id}/data.

payout.description: Payout id (from billetweb_list_payouts) or a date yyyy-mm-dd.

limit.description: Billetweb does not page its lists; at most this many rows are returned (default 200, max 2000); the reply says when it was cut.

updated_since.description: Only contacts changed after this moment.

updated_before.description: Only contacts changed before this moment.

tools.name: billetweb_check_tickets
tools.title: Check tickets in or out
tools.description: WRITE: set the check-in state of tickets (composter): 1 = checked in, 2 = checked out, 0 = back to not checked in. Tickets are identified by the ticket id from billetweb_list_attendees (the `id` field, not the order id). Setting the same state again is harmless. Needs a read+write key. POST /event/{id}/check.

used.description: 0 not checked in, 1 checked in, 2 checked out.

tools.name: billetweb_mark_orders_paid
tools.title: Mark reservations as paid
tools.description: WRITE: confirm the payment of reservation orders (unpaid orders taken as a reservation) with the payment type you were given (card, cash, check, reservation, other). With send_confirmation the BUYER GETS AN EMAIL with the tickets; default is no email. The order id is `order_id` in billetweb_list_attendees. Needs a read+write key. POST /event/{id}/pay_order.

send_confirmation.description: Email the confirmation with the tickets to the buyer (default false).

tools.name: billetweb_send_payment_requests
tools.title: Send payment request emails
tools.description: WRITE: SENDS AN EMAIL to each buyer asking them to pay their unpaid reservation. Customers receive it immediately; it cannot be recalled. The order id is `order_id` in billetweb_list_attendees. Needs a read+write key. POST /event/{id}/pay_request.

tools.name: billetweb_create_offline_orders
tools.title: Create offline orders
tools.description: WRITE: CREATE new orders (tickets) in an event as if sold off-line: each order takes places from the quota and is recorded as paid with the given payment type (card, cash, check, invitation, reservation, other). Only basic tickets (no choice passes, packs or seat placement). With send_tickets the BUYER GETS THE TICKETS BY EMAIL (default: no email). NOT idempotent: calling twice creates two orders, so pass request_id and check billetweb_list_attendees before retrying. Needs a read+write key. POST /event/{id}/add_order.

ticket.description: Ticket type id or exact name (billetweb_list_tickets).

price.description: Custom price (default: the ticket type's price).

request_id.description: Your own id for this ticket, echoed back.

session.description: Session id or start time (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM) for a multi-session event.

language.description: Language of the order, e.g. fr, en.

send_tickets.description: Email the tickets to the buyer (default false).

request_id.description: Your own id for the order, echoed back.
